text: The important word here is movement. Playing centrally does not mean Raphinha has to stand still and wrestle with two centre-backs for ninety minutes. It gives him a starting point from which he can ask different questions. Come towards the ball. Pin a defender for a moment. Then disappear behind his shoulder. Those movements draw on his experience of understanding the game from wide areas. He can recognise the moment a defender turns to look at the ball. That is the moment a run can begin. Think about the difference. Out wide, an attacker often has to beat the defender in front of him before he can threaten the goal. Through the middle, one well-timed movement can put him on the other side of the entire line. Flick has not discovered that Raphinha is a good footballer. We already knew that. He is changing where those qualities hurt you. And that distinction matters. This is a mobile central forward, not a tactical label that explains itself. Watch what he does after taking up the position.
